A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a [[Definition:Probability Space|probability space]] and $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ a [[Definition:Sub-Sigma-Algebra|sub-$\sigma$-algebra]].
Let $X$ be an [[Definition:Integrable Function|integrable]] [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]].
Then there exists a $\GG$-[[Definition:Measurable Function|measurable]] random variable $\expect {X \mid \GG}$, [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Almost Surely|almost surely]], such that:
:$\forall G \in \GG: \displaystyle \int_G \expect {X \mid \GG} \rd \Pr = \int_G X \rd \Pr$

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ be an [[Definition:Integrable Function|integrable]] [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]].
Then its [[Definition:Expectation|expectation]] is the real number:
:$\displaystyle \expect X = \int_\Omega X \rd \Pr$

substitutions.the averaging identity over the whole sp: the averaging identity over every event in G

derived.the defining averaging property: matching integrals against every indicator of a G-event
derived.the trivial sigma-algebra case: recovers the ordinary expectation as a constant

object_map.reformulation: Replace the single summarizing constant by a variable measurable with respect to the available information.

validity_conditions: Taking G to be the trivial sigma-algebra forces the conditional expectation to be constant and reduces the averaging identity to the definition of expectation, so the generalization is faithful.
Existence and almost-sure uniqueness follow from the Radon-Nikodym theorem applied to the measure obtained by integrating X over G-events.
The result is only determined up to sets of probability zero, an ambiguity absent in the unconditional case where the answer is a single number.
proof_plan: Replace the [[Definition:Trivial Sigma-Algebra|trivial $\sigma$-algebra]] $\set {\O, \Omega}$ by an arbitrary [[Definition:Sub-Sigma-Algebra|sub-$\sigma$-algebra]] $\GG$.

A $\set {\O, \Omega}$-measurable function is constant.
Require instead that the summary $Y$ be $\GG$-[[Definition:Measurable Function|measurable]].

Impose:
:$\forall G \in \GG: \displaystyle \int_G Y \rd \Pr = \int_G X \rd \Pr$
For $\GG = \set {\O, \Omega}$ this gives $Y = \expect X$.

Let $\map \nu G = \displaystyle \int_G X \rd \Pr$ for $G \in \GG$.
Then $\nu \ll \Pr \restriction_\GG$.
By the [[Radon-Nikodym Theorem]], $Y = \dfrac {\d \nu} {\d \Pr}$ exists and is unique [[Definition:Almost Surely|almost surely]].
{{qed}}
